say: In 1902 French colonial Hanoi had a brand-new sewer system under the French Quarter (over 19 km by March 1902); brown rats moved into it and were reported climbing up pipes and out of toilets in French homes, during a global bubonic plague pandemic.

From April 1902 the government hired Vietnamese rat catchers to hunt in the sewers, paid per rat; on one day in June 1902 they reported over 20,000 rats killed, yet it made no real dent because rats breed fast.

say: The French then opened the hunt to anyone, with a bounty of 1 cent per rat; to avoid piles of corpses, only the severed tail had to be handed in to the municipal offices. Within weeks large numbers of tails came in.

Officials then saw living rats with no tails: hunters cut off tails and released the rats to breed more; some smuggled rats in from outside Hanoi; health inspectors found rat farms on the outskirts breeding rats for their tails. The bounty made the problem worse and was cancelled.
